 Taylor Ardrey USA TODAY Oct. 20, 2026, 11:23 a.m. ET Hear this story Ford Motor Company is recalling more than 102,000 vehicles due to a defect with the speedometer.
 According to a recent recall notice posted by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the instrument in certain vehicles shows the wrong speed, raising the risk of a crash.
 "The analog cluster’s tachometer and speedometer may become stuck or move erratically, providing inaccurate readings to the driver," the notice says.
 Here's what we know about the recall and what car owners should do next.
 More car recalls: Hyundai recalls 94K vehicles over fire risk. See affected models Which models are included in the Ford recall?
 According to the NHTSA, 102,159 vehicles are potentially affected. The models included are:
 2026 Ford F-150
 2025-2026 Ford D-250 SD
 2025-2026 Ford F-350 SD
 2025-2026 Ford F-450 SD
 2025-2026 Ford F-550 SD
 2025-2026 Ford F-600 SD
 2026 Ford F-750 SD
 The recall number is 26C46. According to the safety report, an indicator of the issue is: "Customers with a redundant digital speedometer function available in the cluster may notice a difference between the 2 speeds displayed."

 Car owners are advised to take their vehicle to the dealership, where the instrument cluster modules will be replaced at no charge.
 Letters about the safety risk are set to be mailed on Oct. 26. An additional notification will be sent in December.
 Ford can be reached at 866-436-7332.
